name: Uses Action
description: A declared job calls an action with `uses:`, handing that action its token, its checkout and every secret in scope. The properties are the pin: a job pinned to a 40-hex commit runs the code it reviewed; a job pinned to a name runs whatever that name points at on the day, which is the mechanism of every tag-repoint compromise in the corpus.

declared_ref.description: The ref exactly as written after the `@` (`v4`, `main`, a 40-hex SHA, a `sha256:` digest); empty when the line names no ref.

pin_kind.description: What kind of thing the declared ref is. `sha` and `digest` are immutable and provable from the string alone. `tag` and `branch` are mutable names whose kind was RESOLVED against the action repository's refs (only possible when that repository is inside the observed scope). `unresolved` is a mutable name whose kind could not be established — the honest value for `actions/checkout@v4` on almost every grid, never guessed as `tag`. `unpinned` means no ref was written.

is_pinned.description: Derived: true iff `pin_kind` is `sha` or `digest`. The one-bit answer to the question every action-pinning control asks; carried explicitly so a view does not re-derive it three ways.

resolved_sha.description: The commit the declared ref resolved to at collection time: the SHA itself for a `sha` pin, the ref's head commit for an in-scope `tag`/`branch`, absent otherwise. Field history on this value across collections is the tag-repoint detection.

resolution.description: How `pin_kind` and `resolved_sha` were established. `literal`: read off the string (a SHA or digest). `in_scope`: resolved against refs the collector holds for the action's own repository. `unobservable`: the action lives outside the observed scope and no call was made to look — absence of a resolved SHA here is NOT evidence of anything.

step_indexes.description: Every step position in the job that uses this action at this ref, in file order. Steps are not nodes (rejected on the node test), so this is where a step-level fact lives.
